candidates.title: A product alpha 2.1 kept with a category in its own words vanishes from every head door after the upgrade
candidates.area: upgrade path: catalogues (alpha 2.1 rows read at the head)
candidates.statement: After the upgrade the head leaves out, with no word to the person, every product alpha 2.1 kept with a category outside the twelve classes the head now types, so the catalogue list, the entry's own read, the catalogues screen and Postdoc's catalogue_read all answer as if the entry were never kept.
candidates.contract: docs/api/intake.md:101 "GET /api/catalogues/{kind} | The entries of strain, product, skill or lesson, by id"; src/screens/Catalogues.tsx:570 "Every entry stays once kept"; docs/decisions/ADR-010-deletions.md:10-11 "a person's entry, decision or artifact on a live instance is never deleted by this build"
candidates.reproCommand: bash bughunt/notes/H6/scripts/repro_h6_01.sh (needs the wt-main worktree at 112eb8b with its venv, as notes.md says)
candidates.expected: The three products alpha 2.1 listed (cellulase, ethanol with category biofuel, xylitol with category sugar alcohol written by alpha 2.1's own catalogue_write tool) still listed and readable by id at the head, or each named with why on the screen as GET /api/state names a row it cannot read in `refused`.
candidates.observed: alpha 2.1 lists ['cellulase','ethanol','xylitol']; after pnpm db:migrate the head lists ['cellulase']; GET /api/catalogues/product/ethanol and /xylitol answer 404 "the project's product catalogue holds no ethanol"; catalogue_read matched 1; the three rows are still in openferment.catalogue; the only trace is a WARNING in the service log. The Products tab draws cellulase alone with no notice (catalogue-products-after-upgrade.png), while the same page's toast names the one state row that does not read. A second project's product (butanol, category solvent) vanished the same way.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/catalogues.py:217 and :277 (alpha 2.2 E.8.2 made `category` a Literal of twelve classes, alpha 2.1 kept any word up to 80 characters) with :401-415 (`_readable` drops a row that does not read and logs it); no migration among 0008-0010 carries or flags the old categories
candidates.evidence: Filled bh_h6_a21 through alpha 2.1's API (its prove.py steps 2-7 plus fill_extra*.py), snapshot.py of every read at alpha 2.1, head migrate, snapshot.py at the head, compare.py/deepdiff.py: the product list is the only read whose rows moved (3 -> 1); repro_h6_01.sh from a fresh database shows the same, log in bughunt/notes/H6/logs/repro_h6_01.log; screens.cjs screenshot 037.

candidates.title: db:import-alpha1 carries a model's estimate into the record store and BioRepo reads it verified, gold
candidates.statement: An alpha 1.0 biorepo.json whose verified decision carries a gold value typed as a model's estimate is carried whole, and BioRepo then serves the record as verified with provenance gold, while the record store's own door refuses the same decision by rule estimate.
candidates.contract: CLAUDE.md:54 (R) "a model estimate never enters a record store, and each store refuses one (ADR-006; core/tests/test_estimates.py, acceptance A6)"; core/openferment_core/import_alpha1.py docstring "The stores' rules are not run again on old records ...; each ran when its record was written" (alpha 1.0's write had no estimate rule to run)
candidates.reproCommand: bash bughunt/notes/H6/scripts/repro_import.sh (case estimate; needs the wt-head worktree at 2047f5a with its venv)
candidates.expected: refused: naming biorepo.json and the decision, nothing written, as biorepo.write refuses it (rule estimate)
candidates.observed: exit 0, 3 decisions carried; GET /api/biorepo/overlay reads cl1-P1-0001 status verified, provenance gold, gold {value 3, unit mg L-1, origin {kind model-estimate, by claude-x}}; POST /api/biorepo/check with the same decision answers ok false, rule estimate
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/import_alpha1.py:174-180 inserts each decision with only provenance_of recomputed; biorepo.write calls basis.refuse_estimates (core/openferment_core/biorepo.py:305) and the import calls nothing of it
candidates.evidence: gen_alpha1.py writes the directory with alpha 1.0's own models (git show alpha-1.0:core/openferment_core/models.py), the estimate case adding an origin to one gold value; run_imports.sh and repro_import.sh run package.json's exact command from a head worktree; logs/imports.log, logs/repro_import.log. A verified decision naming no reviewer is carried the same way (gold, reviewer None), which biorepo.write refuses by rule reviewer.

candidates.title: db:import-alpha1 answers a traceback with no refused: line for a duplicated paper, a missing database and a dead server
candidates.statement: The import prints a Python traceback and exits 1, with no line beginning refused:, when two extraction files name one paper, when the server holds no database of the configured name, and when the server does not answer, where pnpm db:migrate names the last two in words.
candidates.contract: docs/runbooks/live-host-install.md:218-219 "A line beginning `refused:` says why, and the import has written nothing"; core/openferment_core/import_alpha1.py read() docstring "refuse the whole directory, naming the file, when one cannot be read"; core/openferment_core/migrations.py docstring "A command that cannot run says why in words and exits 2"
candidates.reproCommand: bash bughunt/notes/H6/scripts/repro_import.sh (cases dup-paper, a database the server does not hold, a server that does not answer)
candidates.expected: refused: in words, exit 2, naming the second extraction file for the paper, or the database and server as db:migrate names them
candidates.observed: dup-paper: exit 1, 3 tracebacks ending in UniqueViolationError pk_candidates (project, P1, model); missing database: exit 1, DBAPIError traceback; dead server: exit 1, ConnectionRefusedError traceback. pnpm db:migrate on the same two addresses answers "refused: the server at 127.0.0.1:5432 holds no database bh_h6_nothere ..." and "refused: the database bh_h6_x on 127.0.0.1:8869 could not be reached". Nothing is written in any case (the transaction rolls back).
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/import_alpha1.py:242 catches ImportRefused, ProjectRefused and DatabaseUnavailable alone, read() never checks paperIds across candidates/*.json, and alpha 2.2's _unreadable words (migrations.py) were given to db:migrate alone
candidates.evidence: logs/imports.log and logs/repro_import.log; the duplicated paper is a copy of candidates/P1.json under another file name, as a file manager's duplicate makes it

candidates.observed: printed "3  people"; kept 2 (p-ada Ada Moreno, p-ben Ben Ortiz (again)); the import_alpha1 audit row's detail.counts.people is 3
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/import_alpha1.py:79 counts the entries of each file; rows.put (db/rows.py) upserts by (project_id, id)

candidates.title: ADR-001 and CLAUDE.md say a row's body is JSONB; every content column is json
candidates.statement: ADR-001's implementation note and CLAUDE.md's architecture line say the Pydantic model is kept as a JSONB body, and the migrations make every content column (34 of them) of type json, as models.py's own docstring says it chose.
candidates.contract: docs/decisions/ADR-001-postgresql.md:62 "the rest of the row is `body`, the Pydantic model of `models.py` dumped as JSONB"; CLAUDE.md:66 "the Pydantic model as JSONB `body` (ADR-001)"
candidates.expected: jsonb columns, or the two documents saying json as core/openferment_core/db/models.py:6-9 does
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/db/models.py:36 imports postgresql JSON; db/alembic/versions/0001_initial.py and 0006-0010 make postgresql.JSON columns
candidates.evidence: check_jsonb.sh on a database migrated from empty; compare_metadata shows the models and migrations agree with each other (migrate_checks.log)

suspected.title: alpha 2.1's Proforma runs never replay identically at the head (1 ulp), and runs.md:143 says they replay as they were
suspected.tried: replay_all.py: every alpha 2.1 artifact replayed at the head; all identical but the three proforma.run artifacts (tea.FCI 31220166.41394996 vs 31220166.413949955; withinTolerance false, since a Proforma run registers no tolerance). The same three replayed on a cold alpha 2.1 service also differ, and a Proforma run the head made over the upgraded database replays identically twice, so this reads as BioSTEAM's worker-state dependence (the known A-B-A drift); nothing here ties it to the upgrade.
